title: ARC Scaling Challenge: An Open Falsification Toolkit for Recursive-Amplification Scaling Laws
description:
Can you falsify the ARC Principle?

The ARC Principle proposes that recursive self-correction on structured asymmetry produces super-linear capability gains:

U = I × R^α

where α = 1/(1-β)

This repository provides standardised tools for researchers to:
1. Measure α in their own systems
2. Compare results across domains
3. Falsify the framework if it fails

The toolkit provides alpha/beta estimators, AIC/BIC model selection, falsification criteria, reproducible protocols, and synthetic example data.

The robust, replicated finding is that the FORM of recursion governs the scaling exponent (parallel alpha ≈ 0; sequential super-linear within architecture); an early single-model estimate (alpha ≈ 2.24) is retracted, having failed to replicate cross-architecturally (cross-architecture fit ≈ 0.49).

Independent corroboration (sequential > parallel)
The central prediction tested by this toolkit (sequential recursion gives α > 1, parallel gives α < 1) is independently corroborated by:
Sharma, A. & Chopra, P. (2025). The Sequential Edge: Inverse-Entropy Voting Beats Parallel Self-Consistency at Matched Compute. arXiv:2511.02309 (4 November 2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02309
The sequential-beats-parallel result is independently corroborated by Sharma & Chopra (arXiv:2511.02309, 2025) and no priority is claimed for it; the bare d/(d+1) exponent is acknowledged prior art.

We welcome falsification. Either outcome advances science.
